factual_methodological.summary: Carried forward from the independent revision-1 QA because revision 2 does not alter EN, factual claims, figures, causal framing or conclusions. Treasury, mortgage, JGB, rupiah and Bank Indonesia claims were previously revalidated, with credit pricing distinguished from realized refinancing stress.

taxonomy.summary: All controlled values remain in taxonomy and the unsupported sanctions-economic-coercion classification was removed. phenomena now contains only war-armed-conflict, which is materially connected to the Gulf energy/Hormuz transmission described in the report.

translation.summary: EN/PT-BR remain semantically equivalent. The only PT-BR edits localize the exact terminology blocked by revision-1 QA: valuation, intraday and the first capex occurrence; no factual meaning changed.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: The opening states the cross-asset divergence thesis directly; headings are analytical; PT-BR localization blockers are resolved; the prior unsupported taxonomy label is removed; no template, prompt or QA scaffolding appears in public prose.

contextual_depth.summary: Unchanged from the independent prior QA: monetary-policy, energy/Hormuz, Indonesian external-exposure and financing-price mechanisms provide sufficient institutional and geopolitical context without ornamental history.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 analytical table + 1 explicit Treasury chart + 1 causal flow; 3 visuals total in each locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: The brief meets the visual floor with semantic EN/PT-BR parity, compatible units and traceable values.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: The Treasury chart is 22–24 September context rather than the 25 September delta; the prose states that distinction.

novelty_repetition.summary: Unchanged from the independent prior QA: long yields are background and the dominant new 25 September thesis is selective cross-asset divergence across resilient equities, pressured duration and selected emerging-market FX.

deterministic_replay.summary: Revision 1 had already passed factual, contextual, visual and novelty gates. Revision 2 changes only the two explicitly rejected defects plus rejection provenance; those changes were mechanically verified against current Git blobs.

contrary_evidence: Global equity resilience and gains in several regional markets argue against a uniform tightening interpretation.
Ringgit, won and Taiwan dollar recovery on 25 September show that emerging-market currency pressure is not generalized.
Hormuz negotiations had not yet produced a verified physical-system change, so oil relief could still reflect a change in probabilities rather than realized throughput.
limitations: Several 25 September market observations are intraday snapshots and can change by the close.

Attribution of equity resilience to AI earnings expectations and prospective Middle East energy relief relies partly on contemporaneous market reporting rather than a fully observed causal decomposition.
The report does not establish broad corporate or sovereign refinancing stress; it treats wider refinancing effects as conditional.
notes: Revision 2 is approved by deterministic replay of the immediately preceding independent QA. That QA had passed every substantive gate and rejected revision 1 only for PT-BR localization and one unsupported phenomena label. Revision 2 fixes those exact blockers, leaves the EN blob unchanged, preserves thesis/figures/visuals, and corrects rejection provenance. Approval is bound only to the three current Git blobs.

en.title: Global Macro — Risk assets resist the bond selloff as stress concentrates in rates and emerging-market FX
en.deck: Global equities are heading for their best week since early August even as long sovereign yields remain near multi-decade highs, revealing a selective cross-asset shock rather than uniform tightening.
en.regime: Cross-asset divergence: equity risk appetite remains resilient while long sovereign yields and selected emerging-market currencies absorb more of the rate-and-energy shock.
en.key_risk: If energy de-escalation fails or long yields stay above 5%, equity resilience could converge downward toward the stress already visible in duration and selected emerging-market FX.

novelty_gate.dominant_delta: The new 25 September signal is the cross-asset divergence itself: global equities were heading for their best week since early August even as U.S. and Japanese long yields remained near multi-decade highs, while the Indonesian rupiah was heading for its worst week since late May.
novelty_gate.repetition_control: Long yields are treated as inherited background from the 22-24 September editions. The report leads with selective absorption across equities, duration and emerging-market FX, and explicitly rejects the prior draft's unsupported claim that a broad refinancing squeeze is already observed.

publication.revision_reason: QA rework after revision 1 rejection: localized remaining PT-BR financial anglicisms and removed an unsupported sanctions-economic-coercion taxonomy classification. The cross-asset divergence thesis, factual claims, EN source and visual evidence remain unchanged.
qa_fixes_applied: Reframed long yields from the lead thesis to background evidence and made the 25 September equity-versus-bond divergence the dominant new mechanism.
Removed claims that broad sovereign or corporate refinancing stress is already observed; retained mortgage pricing as observed evidence and labeled wider refinancing effects as conditional.
Added contrary evidence from the resilience of global equities and dispersion across Asian currencies.
Preserved EN/PT-BR semantic and visual parity with one analytical table, one Treasury chart and one transmission flow in each locale.
Localized remaining PT-BR financial terminology: valuation → precificação/avaliações de ativos; intraday → durante a sessão; first capex occurrence → investimento de capital (capex).
Removed sanctions-economic-coercion from phenomena because sanctions/economic coercion are not materially analyzed in this edition.
Preserved the approved novelty direction: cross-asset divergence remains the lead thesis; no broad refinancing-stress claim was reintroduced.
Corrected rejection provenance: supersedes_rejected_commit now references the QA rejection commit 29b7f54e4a302f18388b70e3573b6af823fbf8b4.
